# Extending glyphome {#extending}

The suite is intentionally open: adding an eleventh module should not
require touching any of the first ten.

## Anatomy of a module

A module is a directory under `packages/` containing:

```
packages/<module>/
├── DESCRIPTION         # standard R package metadata
├── NAMESPACE           # auto-generated from <module>_* exports
└── R/
    └── <module>.R      # palettes, data generators, plot fns, save fn
```

Required public functions:

- `<module>_*_data()` — one or more data generators (synthetic for
  development, real loaders for production).
- `<module>_plot_*()` — one or more plot constructors that return a
  ggplot or patchwork object.
- `<module>_plot_demo()` — convenience entry point returning the
  module's headline figure.
- `<module>_save_demo(output_dir)` — writes the curated figure set to
  `output_dir`.

## Registration

Add the module to `glyphome_modules()` in `R/glyphome-common.R`:

```{r eval=FALSE}
data.frame(
  module    = c(..., "yourmodule"),
  family    = c(..., "your-family"),
  one_liner = c(..., "what your module does in one sentence"),
  n_figures = c(..., 2L)
)
```

After registration, `glyphome_render_all()` will pick up the new module
automatically, the master generator script will render it, and a chapter
slot can be added to `book/_bookdown.yml`.

## Style requirements

- Use `glyphome_theme()` or `glyphome_theme_void()` rather than redefining
  fonts and grids.
- Save with `glyphome_save()` and an explicit `role`.
- Use `patchwork::wrap_plots()` for composition.
- Document every public function with a roxygen2 block.

## Don'ts

- Do not introduce a new categorical palette without checking that it
  reads against the existing module palettes when assembled into a
  manuscript figure.
- Do not depend on heavy bioconductor packages for core rendering. If a
  Bioconductor object is needed, accept the tidy data frame derived from
  it as input.
- Do not bypass the role-based size table to "make a panel bigger".
  Promote the role instead.

## Submitting a module

A new module is accepted into the suite when:

1. Its visual grammar fills a gap not covered by the existing ten.
2. It passes the figure-composition QC checklist (chapter
   \@ref(composing-figures)).
3. It comes with a chapter draft for this book.
4. Its `_save_demo()` runs cleanly via the master generator.
